weekly_thesis: This week made robot intelligence accountable before execution. Across VLAs, world-action models, geometry, safety, and generative models, the repeated question was not whether the final rollout succeeded; it was which observation, contact state, map property, predicate, latent future, or scenario condition had authority to change or veto the next action. For APRL, the defensible asset is a shared evidence-gated evaluation protocol that connects VLA adaptation, contact forecasting, map degeneracy, scenario-conditioned policy confidence, and process-valid generated worlds in the same closed-loop episodes.

clusters.cluster: VLA control shifts from policy outputs to runtime authority interfaces
clusters.why_it_matters: The week repeatedly exposes a measurable interface that can change a VLA action before terminal success is known: tool use, counterfactual recovery, skill-block composition, closed-loop code replanning, self-demonstrated adaptation, continual skill subspaces, and latent-action choices. This turns VLA evaluation from a single success rate into an authority audit over who may rewrite, route, adapt, or preserve an action.
clusters.confidence: High - every weekday contributed a distinct VLA or robot-learning paper that localizes execution authority.
clusters.lab_action: Run the same tabletop and mobile-manipulation perturbations through tool-use, recovery, skill-library, code-replanning, self-demonstration, skill-subspace, and latent-action variants; score next-action delta, old-skill forgetting, intervention timing, and clean-task success.

paper_autopsies.title: Imagining Recovery: Inference-Time Counterfactual Realignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: A deployed VLA is usually expected to continue from the current observation or require failure data, retraining, or an external recovery agent.
paper_autopsies.friction: Mid-episode goal changes, scene perturbations, and robot-state deviations can break a frozen policy even when a recent viable state still exists.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A synthetic continuation from a viable state can supply enough evidence to realign the physical robot without unsafe trial-and-error.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Treat recovery as counterfactual realignment: imagine the nominal continuation, minimally move robot and scene back onto it, then return control to the frozen policy.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract describes detecting deviation, synthesizing observations from a recent viable state, and realigning the robot and scene before policy handoff.

decisive_evidence.claim: CoRe is a training-free framework that recovers a frozen VLA at inference time without failure data.
The authors report improved success and reduced physical restorations across simulators, VLA backbones, and real-world settings.
APRL should measure whether imagined recovery changes the next action before more physical correction is attempted.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If counterfactual continuations only help small geometric perturbations but fail under contact-rich state uncertainty, the recovery authority is narrower than the headline suggests.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Stress false deviation detection, ambiguous viable states, and cases where the imagined observation is plausible but contact state is wrong.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Recover by testing the action path that should have happened, not by immediately retraining or handing control away.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for frozen VLA deployment with recoverable state deviations; weaker where the viable state is not observable or safe to reconstruct.

paper_autopsies.title: Teach and Grow: An Agent-Centered Architecture for General Robot Learning
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Generalist VLA or world-action policies are often treated as monolithic models that must be retrained when physical coverage is missing.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract frames unfamiliar objects, sensors, embodiments, and contacts as a recurring retraining tax because embodied data must be created by operating machines.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Reusable closed-loop skill blocks can reduce the need to regenerate robot data when a new scene only requires recomposition or routing.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Shift the unit of learning from one end-to-end policy to an agent that builds, grounds, composes, and revises executable Skill Blocks.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract describes converting a few successful demonstrations into subgoal behaviors, then grounding and composing them with learned or geometric tools while observing physical outcomes.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper names the retraining tax as the cost of collecting new robot data, updating policy, and regression testing after coverage failure.
It proposes a Skill Library of executable closed-loop behaviors for meaningful subgoals.
APRL should evaluate whether a skill-block library reduces new-data burden under object, sensor, and contact shifts.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If most new scenes still require new physical data and policy updates, the architecture has not reduced the retraining tax.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Stress compositional tasks where a reused block is locally successful but globally violates the instruction or contact constraint.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Measure reuse as physical coverage expansion, not as a larger prompt or longer policy trace.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for modular manipulation and navigation skills; weaker when the task requires a genuinely new contact primitive.

paper_autopsies.title: MANIGUARD: A Benchmark and Data Suite for Specification-Grounded Safety Evaluation and Improvement of Robotic Manipulation
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Manipulation policies are commonly ranked by task success, while safety is inferred from aggregate behavior or learned judges.
paper_autopsies.friction: A robot can complete a task while violating a contact, ordering, or workspace constraint that should have been specified independently.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Safety must be monitored by explicit physics-grounded predicates while task success and OOD perturbation are held apart.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Make safety specification an independent evaluation object with locked tasks, single-axis perturbations, and runtime automaton monitors.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract describes 200 locked base tasks, four OOD perturbations per task, and LTLf-grounded automaton monitors over physics-grounded predicates.

decisive_evidence.claim: The benchmark organizes contact-rich household manipulation into a skill by constraint taxonomy.
Each task is evaluated under one in-distribution and four single-axis OOD perturbations with the safety specification fixed.
APRL should require safety predicates that can fail even when final task success is true.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If predicate violations do not predict real robot damage, instability, or operator rejection, the specification is too formal but not physical enough.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Stress policies that exploit simulator tolerances, graze forbidden objects, or satisfy a goal after a transient unsafe contact.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Separate task success from specification satisfaction before ranking robot policies.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation with clear physical predicates; less direct for open-ended social or language-only safety claims.

paper_autopsies.title: GS-VLA: Plug-and-Play Viewpoint Canonicalization for Frozen VLA Policies via Gaussian Splatting
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Frozen VLA policies are often evaluated as if camera viewpoint is a nuisance handled by data diversity or augmentation.
paper_autopsies.friction: The title frames viewpoint canonicalization as a direct failure interface for frozen policies, which suggests that policy errors can begin before action decoding.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A Gaussian scene representation can normalize viewpoint evidence without changing the policy backbone.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Treat geometry as a plug-in policy-conditioning layer rather than a separate reconstruction artifact.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: Unknown from /pastweek title/subject rows; the safe claim is that Gaussian Splatting is positioned as the canonicalization tool.

decisive_evidence.claim: The title links frozen VLA policies, viewpoint canonicalization, and Gaussian Splatting.
The row is listed under cs.CV with artificial intelligence cross-category context.
Backfill source lacks abstracts, so mechanism and experiment details require later official abstract or PDF reading.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If viewpoint canonicalization improves image alignment but does not change robot action robustness under camera shifts, the policy-facing geometry claim is weak.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Stress the method with calibration error, reflective objects, dynamic distractors, and wrist-camera views where Gaussian geometry may look stable but action evidence is wrong.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Before scaling VLA data, ask whether the camera frame can be canonicalized as a separate intervention.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Most relevant to camera-sensitive manipulation; weaker for policies dominated by force, tactile, or proprioceptive state.

paper_autopsies.title: HiTac-WAM: A Hierarchical Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: World-action models usually predict visual futures and actions, while tactile futures are treated as images or flat latent streams.
paper_autopsies.friction: Contact-rich manipulation can fail because tactile states have physical dependencies that a flat latent may not preserve.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Future touch should be forecast with a hierarchy that reflects contact physics across candidate action chunks.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Move world-action modeling from visual prediction to hierarchical tactile state forecasting.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract describes forecasting future tactile states for candidate action chunks before execution.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper contrasts existing tactile-aware variants with hierarchical physical dependencies.
It forecasts a sequence of future tactile states for each candidate action chunk.
APRL should compare tactile forecast error against contact failure and recovery behavior.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If tactile hierarchy improves prediction but not grasp correction, slip avoidance, or recovery, the world-action value is limited.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Use contact transitions where visual state is stable but force distribution, slip, or deformation changes the correct next action.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Before acting, ask which hidden contact state must be forecast to make the action safe.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for dexterous and deformable manipulation; weaker for navigation tasks without rich contact.

paper_autopsies.title: Evidence-Gated Task and Motion Planning with Vision-Language Models
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: VLM-assisted TAMP can generate plausible subgoals from prior knowledge even when the required object evidence has not been observed.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract warns that under partial observability, unsupported subgoals can cause execution failures or unintended outcomes.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A task planner should gate subgoals on explicit observational support, not only semantic plausibility.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Make evidence availability a hard interface between VLM semantic planning and geometric execution.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract-level mechanism is evidence-gated task and motion planning under partial observability.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper names uncertain availability of goal-relevant objects under partial observability.
It says VLM priors can generate unsupported subgoals that lead to failures or unintended outcomes.
APRL should require a visible evidence gate before geometric planning commits.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If evidence gating only delays execution without reducing unsupported subgoals or failures, the gate is not useful.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Hide goal objects, provide plausible but false priors, and vary when the robot can acquire the decisive observation.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Do not allow semantic priors to become motion goals until observation supports them.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for long-horizon mobile manipulation; weaker for fully observed pick-place.

new: Friday added explicit evidence-gated TAMP and class-conditional VLM coverage to the week-long evidence-authority theme.
Whole-body and tactile world-action models made hidden contact and base-arm factorization more explicit than earlier weekly artifacts.
strengthening: Runtime interfaces repeated all week: tool use, counterfactual recovery, process rewards, code replanning, self-demonstration, latent actions, and safety gates.
Robot-usable geometry strengthened through Gaussian scene memory, MotionGS-SLAM, uncertainty-aware SLAM, bundle-adjustment validity, GS-VLA, and degeneracy-aware LiDAR odometry.
commoditizing: Generic VLA scaling, generic video realism, and generic reconstruction quality look less defensible unless they expose an action-relevant evidence variable.
contradiction: Flexible VLA behavior wants broad semantic transfer, while evidence gates, safety predicates, and scenario conditioning deliberately restrict when actions are allowed.
missing_axis: No single benchmark yet ties VLA adaptation, evidence-gated planning, tactile forecasting, and map degeneracy into one closed-loop robot episode.

strategy_board.why_now: Every weekday produced a paper that asks which cue, predicate, memory, map, or latent is allowed to authorize an action.
strategy_board.contrarian_bet: APRL should own the authorization protocol instead of competing first on another VLA backbone.
strategy_board.one_week_probe: Create ten mobile-manipulation episodes with hidden objects, cue conflicts, safety predicates, and map degeneracy labels.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Evaluate VLM-TAMP, VLA, tool-use, safety-shield, and map-aware policies with shared authorization traces.
strategy_board.success_metric: Evidence labels predict or prevent at least three unsupported actions before terminal failure while preserving clean-task success.
strategy_board.stop_condition: If authorization labels do not change policy ranking or recovery choice, split into planning-only and perception-only tracks.
strategy_board.paper_path: Evidence-gated execution for reliable mobile manipulation.
strategy_board.asset_path: APRL evidence-gated episodes with observations, predicates, map states, action deltas, and recovery outcomes.

strategy_board.why_now: HiTac-WAM, DECOWAM, surgical WAM, DA-WAM, and safety JEPA make future-state quality accountable to candidate actions.
strategy_board.contrarian_bet: Treat hidden tactile and body-state forecasts as the moat, not video fidelity or generic latent prediction.
strategy_board.one_week_probe: Instrument one door traversal, one dexterous grasp, and one base-arm task with tactile, ego-motion, and action-chunk labels.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Compare tactile WAM, whole-body WAM, decision-aligned latent, and action-conditioned safety models under matched episodes.
strategy_board.success_metric: A hidden forecast variable predicts next-action correction or safety veto earlier than visual future quality.
strategy_board.stop_condition: If hidden forecasts do not improve action correction beyond previous-action baselines, reduce scope to tactile-only tasks.
strategy_board.paper_path: Pre-commit world-action evidence for contact-rich mobile manipulation.
strategy_board.asset_path: Tactile traces, ego/arm action factors, action chunks, latent futures, and recovery labels.

strategy_board.why_now: The week connected geometry to policy viewpoint, scale, localizability, registration transfer, and route recovery.
strategy_board.contrarian_bet: Avoid rendering-fidelity competition by owning the validity tests that determine whether a map can guide a robot.
strategy_board.one_week_probe: Record two corridor and tabletop scenes with scale drift, repeated structure, dynamic objects, and camera shifts.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Compare LiDAR odometry, monocular SLAM, Gaussian maps, BA, and registration systems on the same downstream route or grasp tasks.
strategy_board.success_metric: A geometry validity metric predicts route or grasp failure better than photometric, APD, or optimizer scores.
strategy_board.stop_condition: If validity metrics do not change downstream decisions, narrow the claim to localization diagnostics.
strategy_board.paper_path: Operational validity tests for robot geometry and SLAM.
strategy_board.asset_path: Scale ground truth, localizability fields, registration shifts, pose failures, and task outcome logs.
